estorage-terminal-view-tip: Switch between what is stored and what can be crafted
estorage-import-hint: An empty filter takes everything. Otherwise only the listed types.
estorage-export-hint: Pushes only filter types into the facing inventory.
estorage-storage-hint: The facing chest shows in the terminal. An empty filter shows everything.
estorage-interface-hint: The top row sets what to keep; the sample is not consumed. Arrows lead to the row under it, which places items into the machine. The bottom row holds patterns.
block-handbooktext-estoragechest: One disk and a terminal. Sneak to insert or remove the disk. A normal click opens the network.
block-handbooktext-estoragemonitor: Shows the network craft queue. Cancel clears it.
block-handbooktext-estorageemitter: Compares how many of an item are in the network with a threshold. An import or export bus beside it runs only while the emitter is on.
block-handbooktext-estoragewireless: The wireless terminal opens the network within 32 blocks while this block has a channel and the controller has power.
block-handbooktext-estoragep2p: Sneak cycles frequency 1–8. Two blocks on the same frequency: the input uses 1 channel and the output provides 32 more.
estorage-assembler-hint: The interface puts a pattern's ingredients here. The craft finishes on its own and the result returns to the network.
estorage-assembler-idle: Waiting for a pattern from the interface
estorage-craft-missing: Not enough items for this craft
estorage-craft-tool: Recipes with a tool or a returned item are not supported yet
estorage-craft-grid: Place the held item itself. The next craft takes the same set from the network when the network has all of it.
estorage-craft-out: Take the craft. Whatever the grid is short, the terminal takes from the network. Shift repeats while a full set remains.
estorage-craft-hands: The cursor is holding something else
estorage-pattern-hint: The bottom encodes a pattern: grid, arrow, and output. Mode buttons sit above the output. To the right: the blank pattern, the down arrow, and the finished pattern.
estorage-pattern-blank: Blank. Encode a recipe in the pattern terminal.
estorage-pattern-noblank: Put a blank pattern in the left slot of the encode block
estorage-pattern-outputfull: The second slot has no room for a different pattern
estorage-pattern-craft-tip: Crafting: the workbench grid and one output cell from the recipe
estorage-pattern-process-tip: Processing: three output cells to the right of the grid. No grid recipe is required
estorage-pattern-substitute-tip: Substitution: the pattern is marked so similar items can stand in
estorage-pattern-out: The encoded pattern comes out here
estorage-pattern-needout: Put a product in the processing output cells
estorage-bus-nolink: No inventory on the facing side
estorage-nopower: No power. Connect the controller to a 128 V line
estorage-nocontroller: No controller. Link the blocks with network cable
estorage-conflict: Two controllers are on the same network
estorage-disk-hint: Insert into a drive. Items are accessed from a terminal.
estorage-part-split: An empty one in the crafting grid, or a sneak-use, returns the housing and the component.
item-handbooktext-estoragediskhousing: With a disk component of the same tier this becomes a disk. Put the component in the middle of the housing grid, or combine it with a finished housing.
item-handbooktext-estoragecellhousing: With a cell component of the same tier this becomes a liquid cell. Put the component in the middle of the housing grid, or combine it with a finished housing.
item-handbooktext-estoragecomponent: Disk memory. 1k is network cable, clear quartz, an anode, and resistors. 4k is three 1k components and smoky quartz. 16k is three 4k components and rose quartz. 64k is three 16k components and an amethyst.
item-handbooktext-estoragecellcomponent: Liquid-cell memory, separate from disks. 1k is anodes, clear quartz, resistors, and a bucket. 4k is three 1k components and smoky quartz. 16k is three 4k components and rose quartz. 64k is three 16k components and an amethyst.
item-handbooktext-estoragedisk: A disk housing plus a disk component of the same tier. A drive holds up to 63 item types on it. An empty disk in the crafting grid returns the housing and leaves the component in its place. Sneak-use does the same.
item-handbooktext-estoragecell: A cell housing plus a cell component of the same tier. A drive holds up to four liquids on one shared volume. An empty cell in the crafting grid returns the housing and leaves the component in its place. Sneak-use does the same.
estorage-cell-hint: Insert into a drive. Liquid is accessed from the liquid terminal.
block-handbooktext-estoragecontroller: Heart of the network. Controllers that share a face are one multiblock: each block adds 32 channels. A second controller reached only by cable breaks the network. A cable strand passes 8, and four strands pass 32. One 128 V connection powers the whole network. Draw is paid once: 8 W idle, plus 10 W per drive, 6 W per terminal, 4 W per bus, 6 W per interface, 8 W per assembler, 6 W per exchange port and 2 W per inserted disk or cell. How to build the network is in the guide.
block-handbooktext-estoragecable: Sits on a solid face, the same way an electrical wire does. Another click adds a segment; breaking removes the segment under the cursor. It does not carry electricity. Clicking a segment that is already there adds a strand, up to four. One strand passes 8 channels per controller, and each extra strand adds 8. Each device uses one. Terminals, the interface and buses clip onto a strand. More is in the guide.
block-handbooktext-estoragedrive: Ten slots for disks and liquid cells. Items are taken from the terminal, liquid from the liquid terminal. A removed disk or cell keeps its contents. A disk is a disk housing plus a disk component. A cell is a cell housing plus its own cell component.
block-handbooktext-estorageterminal: Attaches to a network cable, on the face that holds a strand. Access every disk on the network while the controller has power. Left click takes a stack, right click takes one. Shift moves items between the terminal and your inventory. Several terminals can share one block, one on each face. The button on the right switches Stored and Can craft. The mouse wheel on an item that has a pattern opens the order.
block-handbooktext-estorageliquidtermina: Mounts the same way as the item terminal. Shows liquid stored on cells in the drives. A bucket, bowl, or jug pours the whole stack on left click and one litre from a single container on right click. An empty stack on a slot fills every container, and right click fills one litre into one container. A liquid portion can also be moved like an item. One cell holds up to four liquids and they share the litres: 1k stores 8192 litres, and each tier holds four times more. The same Stored / Can craft button sits on the right. The mouse wheel on a liquid that has a pattern opens the order.
block-handbooktext-estorageimport: A flat panel. Lay a network cable on a chest, barrel, quern, or assembler first, then clip the bus onto that wire. While the controller has power and the bus has a channel, it pulls items into the network. Right click opens the filter: empty takes everything, otherwise only the sample types. Samples are not consumed. One channel, 4 W.
block-handbooktext-estorageexport: A flat panel. Lay a network cable on a chest, barrel, quern, or assembler first, then clip the bus onto that wire. While the controller has power and the bus has a channel, it pushes network items that match the filter. With an empty filter it pushes nothing. Samples are not consumed. One channel, 4 W.
block-handbooktext-estorageioport: Four slots. A disk or a cell in the port is not part of the network. Each slot moves 32 items or 32 litres at a time. Sneak, or the button in the window, reverses the direction and fills the part from the network. One channel, 6 W.
block-handbooktext-estoragestorage: Place it against a chest, on the face you click. While the controller has power that chest is visible in the terminal and can be withdrawn from there. New deposits fill disks first; the overflow goes into the chest. An empty filter allows every type, otherwise only the samples.
block-handbooktext-estorageinterface: A flat panel. Lay a network cable on a chest, barrel, quern, or assembler first, then clip the interface onto that wire. Three rows. The top row sets what to place and how many: the sample is not consumed. Arrows lead to the row under it, which places items into the input of the block it is mounted on; the network fills that row. The bottom row holds encoded patterns. Every terminal has a Stored / Can craft button for the pattern result. The mouse wheel on that item opens the order: choose a quantity and press Next, and the window shows the craft tree and how many items will be taken from the network. Order takes one free processor for the whole craft tree; otherwise it says there are no free CPUs. The interface feeds the ingredients into the input and pulls the output until the order is filled. On an assembler, a craft pattern is made in its grid. One channel, 6 W.
block-handbooktext-estorageassembler: An interface mounts on its face. A craft pattern goes into the grid all at once, once there are enough ingredients for one craft. The assembler makes the workbench recipe and returns the result to the network. Several interfaces on one assembler take turns. A processing pattern does not use it: that still feeds a machine. It uses no channel. 8 W while an interface is mounted. A craft takes about eight seconds and draws 32 W while it runs. The bar pauses without power. A container of liquid in the pattern stays as it is on the workbench. The processor reserves the required litres from the liquid network for the order, and the assembler does not spend the container.
block-handbooktext-estoragepatterntermin: Mounts like the item terminal and shows the network. The bottom is a workbench grid: crafting has one recipe output, processing has three. A plain arrow sits between the grid and the output. Mode buttons sit above the output. To the right: the blank pattern, the down arrow, and the finished pattern. Items in the grid are not consumed. Substitution marks the pattern. The network list has the same Stored / Can craft button. The mouse wheel on an item that has a pattern opens the order.
block-handbooktext-estoragecraftterminal: Mounts like the item terminal and shows the network. The bottom is a workbench grid: the held item itself goes into the slots. Take the output once the recipe matches: the grid spends those items, and the next set is taken from the network when the network has the whole set. Shift repeats while a full set remains and the inventory has room. Clear every grid slot to forget the recipe. This is not an order through a processor. One channel, 6 W. The same Stored / Can craft button sits on the right. The mouse wheel on an item that has a pattern opens an order through a processor.
block-handbooktext-estorageprocessor: Stores the items set aside for a craft order. Memory matches a disk: 1k, 4k, 16k or 64k. Processors in a solid rectangle become one block and add their memory together. Until the rectangle is complete, each block stays its own processor. One order per block: the whole tree, intermediates included, stays on that processor. An order from the terminal shows the craft tree and what will be taken from the network. The order does not start without a free processor. If the whole order does not fit, the largest free processor stores what it can. A rectangle uses one channel, and each block draws 4 W. The 4k, 16k and 64k are a disk of that size, anodes, and a quartz (smoky, rose, amethyst) on the next smaller processor. The 64k also takes two temporal gears. Right click opens the craft status.
block-handbooktext-estoragestock: Put a sample in the slot. Shows how many of that item are in the network. Take and sneak give one stack. Craft orders a stack when a pattern exists.
estorage-cell-hint: Left click takes a stack, right click takes one.
blockdesc-estoragecable: Network cable. Terminals, the interface and buses clip onto a strand.
blockdesc-estoragecontroller-*: Heart of the network. Runs on 128 V and hands out channels.
blockdesc-estoragedrive-*: Ten slots for disks and liquid cells.
blockdesc-estorageterminal: Network screen. Clips onto a cable strand.
blockdesc-estorageliquidterminal: Screen for the network liquids. Clips onto a cable strand.
blockdesc-estoragepatternterminal: Encodes patterns. Clips onto a cable strand.
blockdesc-estoragecraftterminal: A workbench fed by the network. Clips onto a cable strand.
blockdesc-estorageinterface: Places items into a machine and holds patterns. Clips onto a cable strand.
blockdesc-estorageimport: Pulls items from a chest or a machine into the network. Clips onto a cable strand.
blockdesc-estorageexport: Pushes items from the network into a chest or a machine. Clips onto a cable strand.
blockdesc-estorageioport-*: Moves a disk or a cell into the network and back.
blockdesc-estorageassembler: Crafts a workbench recipe from an interface pattern.
blockdesc-estorageprocessor-*: Memory for one order. A rectangle of blocks adds their capacity together.
itemdesc-estoragedisk-*: Stores items in a drive. An empty one can be taken apart.
itemdesc-estoragecell-*: Stores liquids in a drive. An empty one can be taken apart.
itemdesc-estoragediskhousing: Disk housing. A disk component goes in the middle.
itemdesc-estoragecellhousing: Cell housing. A cell component goes in the middle.
itemdesc-estoragepattern: A recipe pattern. A blank one is encoded in the pattern terminal.
estorage-guide-text:
Storage network
Items sit on disks and liquids sit in cells. Both go into a drive. The network cable carries no electricity: only channels travel along it. 128 V on one controller feeds the whole network. Controllers that share a face are one multiblock, and each block adds 32 channels. A second controller reached only by cable breaks the network.

Channels and draw
One strand passes 8 channels, each further strand another 8, and four strands pass 32. Each device uses one channel. The assembler uses none. A rectangle of processors uses one channel for the whole block. The network is billed once: 8 W on its own, 10 W per drive, 6 W per terminal, 4 W per bus, 6 W per interface, 8 W per assembler while an interface is mounted on it, 6 W per exchange port, 4 W per processor block, and 2 W per inserted disk or cell. While an assembler is crafting, its 8 W becomes 32 W.


The controller is cabled to the drive. Terminals, the interface and the buses clip onto strands of that same cable.

Cable
The cable lays on the face of a solid block, the way a wire does. Another click adds a segment, and a hit breaks the segment under the crosshair. A click on a segment that is already there adds a strand, up to four. Sneak and right click thicken the strand under the crosshair.

A panel does not sit on a bare block. Lay the cable on the chest, barrel, quern or assembler first, then right click the panel onto that strand. Panels in one cell share the faces, one panel per face. The panel faces the face the strand lies on.


The strand lies on the machine face. The panel clips onto the strand and faces that face.

Terminals
All four clip onto a strand. Each uses one channel and draws 6 W.

The terminal opens the items on every disk. Left click takes a stack, right click takes one item. Shift moves between the window and the inventory. The buttons on the right are Stored and Can craft. The mouse wheel on an item that has a pattern opens the order.

The liquid terminal shows the liquid in the cells. A bucket, a bowl or a jug: left click empties the whole stack, right click empties one litre from one vessel. An empty stack on a slot fills completely, and right click pours one litre into one vessel. A portion can be stored and taken as an item. One cell holds up to four liquids, and they share the litres: 1k is 8192 litres, and each next size is four times larger.

The pattern terminal encodes a blank pattern. The grid below is a workbench, and the items in it are not spent. Crafting has one output cell, processing has three. The buttons above the output switch the mode. On the right are the blank pattern, an arrow and the finished pattern.

The crafting terminal is an ordinary workbench: the cells take the item from the hand. When the recipe matches, the output can be taken. The items in the grid are spent, and the next portion is pulled from the network at once if the whole portion is there. Shift repeats the craft while a portion remains and the inventory has room. This is not an order through a processor.

Interface and buses
The interface has three rows. The top row sets what to insert and how much: the sample is not spent. The middle row puts that into the machine input, and the network refills it. The bottom row holds encoded patterns. One channel, 6 W.

The import bus pulls items from a chest or a machine into the network. An empty filter takes everything, otherwise only the listed types. The sample in the filter is not spent. One channel, 4 W.

The export bus pushes into a chest or a machine only what the filter lists. An empty filter pushes nothing. The sample is not spent. One channel, 4 W.

The assembler does not store the recipe itself. An interface on its face places a craft pattern into the grid all at once, once the ingredients for one craft are there. The assembler builds the workbench recipe and returns the result to the network. Several interfaces on one assembler take turns. The assembler does not take a processing pattern: that stays in the interface on the machine itself, for example on a quern. A container of liquid in the pattern stays as it does on the workbench: the processor reserves the required litres, and the assembler does not spend the container. A craft takes about eight seconds. The assembler uses no channel. 8 W while an interface is mounted, and 32 W while it crafts. The bar pauses without power.

Drive and exchange port
The drive has ten slots. A disk holds up to 63 item types, and a cell holds liquids. A disk or a cell that is taken out keeps its contents. Empty ones come apart in the crafting grid and by sneaking while held: the housing and the component of the same size.

The exchange port has four slots. While a disk or a cell sits in the port, its contents are not part of the network. Each slot moves 32 items or 32 litres at a time. Sneak, or the button in the window, reverses the direction and fills the disk or the cell from the network. One channel, 6 W.

Orders
The mouse wheel on an item that has a pattern opens the order window over the terminal: the quantity and the craft tree of what will be taken from the network. Order takes one free processor for the whole tree, including the intermediate crafts. If none is free, the terminal says No free CPUs. If the whole order does not fit, the largest free processor stores what it can.

Processors in a solid rectangle become one block, and their memory adds together. Until the rectangle is complete, each works alone. One order per block. The rectangle uses one channel, and each of its blocks draws 4 W. Right click a processor to open the craft status.

A blank pattern is encoded in the pattern terminal. A craft pattern goes into the interface on the assembler. A processing pattern goes into the interface on the machine itself.


The pattern is encoded in the pattern terminal and placed in the interface. Crafting goes to the assembler, processing goes to the machine. The whole order sits in one processor.
